info.title: Cantara server
info.description: Libraries, designs, running orders and shared presentations for Cantara. See docs/specs/0008-server-version.md in the Cantara repository.

post.summary: A device asks to be logged in.
The device asks whether it has been let in.
Logs in with a password; the answer sets the session cookie.

Creates an account. Open to anybody where registration is open, and to
the holder of an invitation everywhere.

The end of the authorisation flow: a desktop program exchanges the code it
was redirected with, and the verifier only it knows, for a token.

get.summary: What anybody may know about this server.

What an invitation link leads to. Needs no login: it is what is shown
before one.

post.summary: Accepts an invitation for the logged-in account.

get.summary: What a session link leads to. Needs no login.
Who is logged in.

delete.summary:
Deletes the account. What the user stored stays with the organisation it
belongs to, without their name on it.

patch.summary: Changes the user's name or password.

get.summary: Everything the server holds about the user, for taking it elsewhere.
The tokens the user has given to programs.

delete.summary: Takes a token back. The program holding it is logged out.

get.summary: A picture or document of the presentation, for whoever may watch it.

parameters.name: link
parameters.description: A session link, for a viewer who is not logged in.

put.summary:
Hands a picture or document the presentation shows to the server, under
the path the slides name it by. Only for whoever may control the session —
in practice the computer presenting.

parameters.name: link
parameters.description: A session link, for a viewer who is not logged in.

get.summary:
The socket a presenting device, a console or a viewer connects to. The
messages are `SessionServerMessage` and `SessionClientMessage` of the
`cantara-api` crate, as JSON text frames.

parameters.name: link
parameters.description:
The token of a session link. Without one, the user's membership
decides.

get.summary: The tenants the user belongs to — every tenant, for a server admin.

post.summary: Creates a tenant. Only a server admin may, and becomes its first admin.

get.summary: Who a resource is shared with.

post.summary:
Shares a resource with a member or a group of the tenant — or changes how
far an existing share goes.

get.summary: The tenant's groups.

delete.summary: Deletes a group, and whatever was shared with it.

get.summary: Who is in a group.

put.summary: Puts a member of the tenant into a group, or changes their role in it.

delete.summary: Takes somebody out of a group.

get.summary:
The invitations not yet accepted: all of them for an admin, those into
their groups for a manager.

post.summary:
Invites an address. An admin may invite into the tenant and into any
group; a group manager into their group, as a member.

get.summary: The libraries the user may read.

post.summary:
Creates a library. Only admins may; who else may use it is said with
grants afterwards.

get.summary: One library.

delete.summary: Deletes a library with everything in it.

patch.summary: Renames a library or changes its description.

post.summary:
Imports a whole repository from a ZIP, the way `RepositoryType::RemoteZip`
reads one: every file Cantara reads is stored, at its path inside the
archive. An archive whose files all sit in one top folder (a GitHub
download) is read as if that folder were the root.

get.summary:
What is in a library — all of it, or what changed since a revision. This
is the whole of a client's sync.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: The revision the client last saw. Without it, the whole library.

post.summary:
Stores a file: a new item, or a new version of the item it turns out to
be. A multipart form with `file`, and optionally `relative_path` (default:
the file's name) and `base_version`.

get.summary: One item, as it is now.

put.summary:
A new version of a particular item. Like the upload, but the item is
named; `relative_path` moves it.

delete.summary: Removes an item. Its history stays, and it can be restored.

post.summary:
Makes an earlier version the current one again — as a new version, so
that nothing in the history is lost. Also brings back a deleted item.

get.summary: Every version of an item, newest first.

The tenant's members. Every member may see who else is one — they are who
a selection can be shared with.

delete.summary:
Removes somebody from the tenant, its groups, and everything shared with
them there.

patch.summary: Makes a member an admin, or no longer one.

get.summary: The running orders the user may see, the next service first.

post.summary: Saves a new running order, owned by the user.

get.summary: One running order, with everything in it.

put.summary: Saves changes to a running order.

get.summary: The presentations running in the tenant that the user may watch.

post.summary: Opens a session to present into. Whoever opens it owns it.

get.summary: One session.

post.summary:
Replaces both links; whoever held the old ones is shut out from the next
time they connect.

get.summary: The tenant's designs and slide divisions.

post.summary: Adds a design or a slide division.

put.summary: Saves a new version of a design or slide division.

delete.summary: Removes a design or slide division.

get.summary:
The bytes of one version. Never changes, and says so to every cache on
the way; answers range requests, which is what lets a browser seek in a
video.

ApiError.description: What every failed request answers with, whatever its status code.

current_version.description: For a `version_conflict`: the version the item has now.

ApiTokenInfo.description: One of the tokens a user has handed out to programs.

group.description:
The group the invited person joins. Without one they only join the
tenant — which only an admin may invite to.

anonymous_control.description:
Whether somebody holding the control link may control without logging
in. Off by default.

device_code.description: What the device polls with. Secret.

interval.description: Seconds to wait between two polls.

verification_uri_complete.description: The same, with the code already filled in (for a QR code).

DeviceAuthorizationRequest.description:
`POST /auth/device`: a device without a browser of its own asks to be
logged in (RFC 8628). It shows the user code and the address; the user
types the code in on a phone or a computer.

DeviceTokenRequest.description:
`POST /auth/device/token`: the device asks whether the user has said yes.
Until they have, the answer is an [`ApiError`] with the code
`authorization_pending` (or `slow_down`, `expired_token`,
`access_denied`).

grantee_name.description: The user's or group's name, for showing the list.

system.description: The `admins` group. It cannot be renamed or deleted.

GroupRole.description: What somebody is in a group.

ImportReport.description: `POST /tenants/{t}/libraries/{l}/import`: a whole repository as a ZIP.

possible_duplicates.description: Pairs of paths with identical content.

skipped.description: Files in the archive Cantara does not read.

IndexEntry.description:
One item as the index lists it: enough to decide whether the cached copy
is current, and to fetch it when it is not.

lineage.description: The item, across all its versions. A song's `uuid` tag.

relative_path.description: Where the item sits in the library — `Lieder/Amazing Grace.song`.

revision.description: The library revision this entry last changed in.

version.description:
The current version. Never reused: whatever is cached under this id is
exactly what the server has under it.

link.description:
The link to pass on. Only in the answer to creating the invitation —
the server keeps nothing but a hash of it.

mailed.description: Whether the server sent the link by e-mail itself.

InvitationPreview.description: What an invitation link shows before it is accepted.

ItemKind.description: What a file is, in the terms Cantara presents it in.

LibraryIndex.description:
`GET /tenants/{t}/libraries/{l}/index[?since=n]`.

Asked without `since`, it lists every item and `complete` is true. Asked
with the revision a client last saw, it lists only what changed since and
what was removed since; a client applies that to what it has. A server that
cannot answer incrementally (the revision is too old) answers completely.

LibraryInfo.description: A library: what a client shows as one repository.

revision.description: Counts up with every change to the library. See [`LibraryIndex`].

role.description: What the asking user may do with it.

Me.description: `GET /me`: who is logged in, and where they belong.

invitation.description:
The token of an invitation. With one, an account can be created even
where registration is closed — for the address the invitation names.

Role.description:
How far somebody may go with a resource. Each role includes the ones
before it.

base_version.description:
The version this edit started from. A save that names a version the
entry has since moved on from is refused with `version_conflict`.

SelectionDetail.description:
A saved running order.

The manifest is the `selection.json` of a `.cantara.zip` (format
`cantara.selection`), whose items may name a server item by `lineage` and
`item_version` instead of by a file in an archive.

date.description: The day of the service, where the selection is for one.

role.description: What the asking user may do with it.

ServerInfo.description: What anybody may ask a server before logging in: `GET /info`.

name.description: The name the operator gave this server.

oidc_providers.description: The OpenID Connect providers one can log in with.

password_login.description: Whether accounts with a password exist on this server at all.

registration_open.description: Whether people may create an account without an invitation.

sharing_enabled.description:
Whether presentations may be shared through this server. An operator
may switch it off; clients then do not offer it.

single_tenant.description:
Whether this server serves one organisation only. Clients hide the
choice of tenant then.

SessionAccess.description: What a link to a session lets its holder do.

role.description:
What the asking user may do: `read` watches, `write` controls,
`manage` may also share and end it.

running.description: Whether anybody has put a presentation into it yet.

watch_link.description: The links to pass on. Only for somebody who may share the session.

SessionLink.description: `GET /links/{token}`: what a session link leads to.

login_required.description: Whether the holder has to log in before connecting.

SettingsEntry.description:
A design or a slide division the tenant shares.

The body is what the program serialises the setting as. The server does
not look inside it, so a newer program's fields survive an older server.

possible_duplicate_of.description:
Another item of the library with the very same content, if there is
one. Reported rather than merged.

TokenRequest.description:
`POST /auth/token`: the end of the authorisation flow a desktop program
goes through — the code it was handed, and the verifier only it knows.

device_name.description:
What the token is to be called in the list of the user's tokens —
usually the name of the computer.

access_token.description: Sent as `Authorization: Bearer …` from now on. Shown once.

current_password.description: Needed to change the password of an account that has one.

UserInfo.description: A person, as far as anybody else needs to know.

is_server_admin.description:
May create tenants and see every one of them. The account set up from
the server's environment is one.

UserRef.description: A person named as the author of something.

tags.description: The song's tags, where the item is a song.
